steps.instruction: In Grafana, create a NEW dashboard (Dashboards -> New dashboard -> 'Add visualization' or '+ Add panel'). In the panel editor: set the visualization type to 'Stat'. Set the panel title to exactly '{{runid}} Availability'. For the query, select the TestData data source (it may be named 'TestData DB', 'grafana-testdata-app', 'gdevTestData' or similar — pick the TestData one from the data source picker) and leave the default scenario (e.g. 'Random Walk' / 'CSV File') as is. Then click Apply/Back to exit the editor. Then SAVE the dashboard (Save dashboard button or Ctrl+S) with the dashboard title exactly '{{runid}} Bench Dashboard' (rename it in the save dialog or dashboard settings), and confirm the save. Report: the dashboard title shown after saving, the panel title shown on the dashboard, the data source name used, and whether a 'Dashboard saved' confirmation appeared.

steps.instruction: On the Grafana dashboard '{{runid}} Bench Dashboard' (at http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-create.url.p1}}/{{runid}}-bench-dashboard), set the dashboard's auto-refresh interval to '1m' and PERSIST it into the saved dashboard. Approach: open the top-bar refresh interval picker (the one next to the refresh arrow, showing 'Off' by default) and select '1m'. Then, to make sure it is saved into the dashboard, open dashboard Settings (gear) -> General and look for an 'Auto refresh' field / default refresh interval option and set it to 1m if present; then Save (Save dashboard / Save settings) and confirm. If the top-bar refresh picker alone does not produce a saveable change, use the Settings route. Verify a 'Dashboard saved' confirmation appears and that after a fresh reload of the dashboard URL the refresh picker still shows '1m'. Report: the refresh interval shown in the top bar after saving, whether a save confirmation appeared, and what the refresh picker shows after a fresh page load.
